skill.name: runheed
skill.description: Connect Runheed error tracking to a compatible MCP client. Review production errors from Node.js and Python applications, investigate stack traces, and mark errors resolved after deployment.
skill.summary: Review production errors and track their resolution from a compatible MCP client.
skill.author: getrunheed

security_audit.summary: Most matches are reference links, Markdown formatting, or reads of one configuration variable. The setup uses unverified package downloads, exposes a fallback agent key through command arguments, and registers a demo server without separate approval. Production error context and remote tool responses also need explicit data and trust controls.

remediation.issue: Setup installs or runs packages from vendor URLs without documented integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Publish versioned packages with verifiable signatures or digests. Require user approval before installing the SDK or running the local MCP package.

remediation.issue: The local setup asks for an agent key and places it in command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer OAuth. For local setup, have the user enter a scoped key through a supported secret store without exposing it in chat or command arguments.

remediation.issue: A demo request triggers MCP registration without specific approval for the configuration change.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before registering the demo endpoint. Use temporary, isolated configuration where supported and explain how to remove the connection.

remediation.issue: Setup does not define which production error data may leave the application.
remediation.suggestion: Document captured fields and retention. Require approval for each environment, and redact credentials and personal data before sending events.

remediation.issue: The workflow lacks guidance for handling instructions embedded in error reports.
remediation.suggestion: Treat tool descriptions and returned event text as untrusted. Do not follow embedded directions, and require user confirmation before changing incident state.

semantic_findings.title: Production Error Data Shared Without Redaction Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The documented setup reports production failures to a hosted service and exposes stack traces, breadcrumbs, and session context to the agent. These fields may contain sensitive details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill describes automatic reporting and rich error context but gives no pre-ingestion redaction or review steps. The actual SDK filters were not verified.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Error Text Can Influence Agent Actions
semantic_findings.description: The workflow uses remote error details to guide code changes and incident resolution. It does not instruct the agent to treat error content as untrusted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Error text can carry user-controlled strings, and the documented workflow lets returned results guide decisions. No evidence found of an actual injection payload in the skill.

content.value_statement: Pasted stack traces often lack the context needed to diagnose a production error. Runheed lets a compatible MCP client review error occurrences and track their resolution.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve recent errors from a connected Runheed workspace.
Inspect individual occurrences, stack traces, breadcrumbs, and available session context.
Review synthetic errors through the public demo without a paid workspace.
Guide SDK setup for Node.js and Python and verify ingestion with a test event.
Mark a Runheed error resolved after the fix ships.
limitations: Private project monitoring requires a paid Runheed workspace.
Automatic capture uses first-party Node.js and Python SDKs, not browser or mobile SDKs.
Runheed does not provide performance tracing, session replay, or release health.
The skill does not automatically create issues in GitHub, Linear, or Jira.

use_cases.title: Review a Sample Incident
use_cases.description: Use an approved demo connection to see how stack traces and breadcrumbs appear before connecting a real application.

use_cases.title: Check Staging Error Capture
use_cases.description: Verify that a planned test event from a staging application appears in the expected Runheed project.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Error
use_cases.description: Review a recent error and compare occurrences to identify what to investigate before proposing a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Demo Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my existing Runheed demo connection. Summarize one sample error and explain the stack trace in plain language.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a sample without connecting a production project.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Recent Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: List recent Runheed errors for my selected project. Give each error a short summary and omit sensitive values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Get a read-only view of recent project failures.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Error Occurrences
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the stack traces and breadcrumbs for this error. Identify the recurring failure point, separate observations from hypotheses, and suggest a regression test.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate a recurring failure without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Resolution Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the selected incident, its latest occurrences, and the deployment evidence I provided. Recommend a resolution status and wait for my approval before updating Runheed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Decide whether to close an incident after deployment.

output_examples.input: Explain one synthetic error from the connected demo.
output_examples.output: In this sample, the request reaches order validation and stops when a required field is missing. Check where the request supplies that field.

output_examples.input: Summarize what the recent occurrences of this timeout have in common.
output: The reviewed occurrences stop at the same outbound request.
The stack traces show where the timeout surfaced, but not why the upstream service failed.
Check upstream latency and add a regression test for timeout handling.

output_examples.input: Should I resolve this incident after the deployment?
output_examples.output: The latest recorded occurrence predates the deployment. That does not establish that the fix worked. The incident remains unchanged pending verification and your approval.

best_practices: Start with synthetic demo data or an approved staging project before enabling production reporting.
Prefer OAuth and verify package provenance before installing any SDK or local MCP package.
Redact sensitive event fields and confirm deployment before approving an incident status change.
anti_patterns: Pasting agent keys into chat or putting them in command arguments.
Treating text inside stack traces or breadcrumbs as instructions.
Sending production error reports before reviewing what the SDK collects.

faq.question: Can I try Runheed without connecting a production application?
faq.answer: Yes. The public demo uses synthetic errors and does not require an account or paid plan.

faq.question: Which applications have first-party SDKs?
faq.answer: Runheed documents SDKs for Node.js and Python. Other clients can send events to the ingest endpoint without automatic capture.

faq.question: Do I need a paid workspace?
faq.answer: Yes, for monitoring your own projects. The demo is available without a paid workspace.

faq.question: Do I need to share an API key with my coding agent?
faq.answer: No for clients that support the remote MCP connection with OAuth. The documented local fallback requires an agent key.

faq.question: Does Runheed fix and deploy code?
faq.answer: Runheed provides error context and records resolution status. The coding agent and your deployment workflow handle code changes, tests, and release.

faq.question: Does Runheed open tickets in other trackers?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow keeps error triage and resolution in Runheed rather than filing tickets in GitHub, Linear, or Jira.
